title: Taj Mahal - Minotauro - Expéditions Yuc 97/98
credits: Topographie: degré 4 UIS, Expéditions Yuc 97/98 (French cave-diving expeditions; published in Spelunca 1998). North arrow: magnetic north 1997; 200 m scale bar
placementWhy: Moderate (about 20 m; the map is a compilation of several surveys - Taj Mahal, Minotauro, Cuzel - whose relative positions are a little off): free similarity fit on five points, residuals 23, 20, 14, 9 and 8 m; 0.276 m/px (the 200 m scale bar says 0.2685, 3% apart) and 2.8 degrees of rotation, consistent with the 1997 magnetic north (Reato 2013 gives 1.0 deg W, moving 0.13 deg/year). Points: the pond of Taj Mahal and Minotauro's orange pond on their database positions (both Open Caves source, taken on site); Manglar on the ring-shaped pond the placed Gerrard 2001 Taj Mahal map also uses (Mangrova); Mimo Mi on OSM's 'Cenote' pond (way 405950397), the only one in its area; Cuzel's east collapse on OSM's cenote pond (way 405950395, the database's Pakal Nah), as on the placed Yuc 96 Aktun Koh map. Taj Mahal and Minotauro alone give 0.263 m/px and 3.6 deg but put the Cuzel ponds 77-120 m off; on this map Taj - Minotauro is 2% short of the ground, Taj - Cuzel 4% long. Checks: OSM's Minotaur node 9 m; the placed Reato 2013 map's Cenote Estrella 10 m from the small pond its passage ends at here (both maps draw the same passage); the Yuc 96 map's Cénote cultivé (grass-field centre) 57 m, in the west half of the drawn collapse (the Yuc 96 map's own fit has the same problem); the dark pool on the satellite the Gerrard map's City of Agre SW pool is placed on lies just S of Estrela's south tip (34 m from the point checked). Cross-checked against the placed maps: Reato 2013's Minotauro walls run along this map's Minotauro passages (its main N-S trunk 20-40 m W of this one's), its Piedra and Escalera fall on Estrela's east and south lobes, Gerrard's Nachich on its east edge; the Yuc 96 Aktun Koh walls overlap the Cuzel passages.

trace.why: Passages filled in violet-blue (water) and pale cyan (air bells, surface pools), outlined in black; the collapses and ponds (orange, hatched outline, and one dark brown pool) are traced with the passages. The red dots in the passages have no legend: filled over. The white blocks in the passages (Couloir des Géants, Estrela's NW passage...) are kept as details; Estrela's inner hatched slope lines too. The 'Couloir des Géants' and other black labels on the paper picked up a bluish fringe: dropIsolated (250 m2) removes them, while the smallest real isolated part (a pond, 330 m2) stays. The page border is excluded, so the Cuzel passages and the east collapse that run off the top and right edges end on a straight cut.

entrances.name: Vista Bonita (Buena Vista)
entrances.why: The orange pond NW of Taj Mahal: Gerrard 2001's Cenote Buena Vista (same place, 'nice view' in both names; Gerrard's placed map puts it 60 m NE of this pond). The database has Buena Vista in sistema Tajma Ha, without a position.

entrances.name: Estrela (City of Agre)
entrances.why: The large hatched collapse this map calls Estrela is Gerrard 2001's Cenote City of Agre: the placed Gerrard map's City of Agre south-west pool falls 14 m from its south tip, its Nachich on its east edge, as do the Reato 2013 map's Cenotes Piedra and Escalera. Not the Reato map's Cenote Estrella, which is the small pond 70 m south-west (next entrance).

entrances.why: The placed Reato 2013 Minotauro map's Cenote Estrella lands 10 m from it, its passage ending at this pond as here.

entrances.name: Pica Piedra
entrances.why: no entrance drawn: the name labels this isolated 100 m passage S of Estrela; the position is the passage's middle (its cenote could be anywhere along it, about +-50 m). Not in the database. The Reato 2013 map has an isolated passage fragment 40-100 m north of it, perhaps the same cave.

symbols.why: French UIS map (Expéditions Yuc 97/98, the Yuc 96 Aktun Koh map's style): no depths, no letter codes, no legend, no bones, no flow arrows (checked by eye and in the OCR words). Kept as a place name: the Couloir des Géants (giants' corridor, the boulder-strewn passage from Vista Bonita towards Estrela). The orange collapses and ponds are entrances; the red dots in the passages have no legend: not kept.
